networks.definition: The network infrastructure that supports the military departments (Navy, Army, Air Force) and other DoD activities.
Provides operational direction and oversight to the DCS.
networks.hint: DISA directs how the DCS is run.

networks.definition: The day-to-day unclassified, long-haul IP-based network that supports unclassified IP data communications.
A DoD interoperable command-and-control data network used for SECRET traffic and global command and control systems.
Supports Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) with advanced networking for point-to-point or multipoint exchange of voice, text, graphics, data, video, and teleconferencing.

organizations.definition: Trains, certifies, and provides combat-ready Navy forces capable of prompt, sustained naval, joint, and combined operations.
Responsible for cyber-defense functions such as reporting and defending against viruses, phishing, and similar threats.
Associated with communications equipment and circuits — the physical communications material used to support naval communications.

organizations.fullTerm: Naval Computer and Telecommunications Area Master Station
organizations.definition: Operates and maintains responsive information-transfer systems that provide real-time C4I information support to the fleet.
organizations.hint: Area master station for fleet communications.

organizations.definition: Provides Naval IT infrastructure and support services for rapid and reliable voice and data communications within an assigned Area of Responsibility (AOR).
Supports Navy information operations and SIGINT missions.
Watch officer coordinates telecommunications functions ashore and maintains real-time operational status of circuits providing telecommunications.
Helps with network issues; includes regional NOCs such as European, Indian Ocean, Pacific, and unified Atlantic.
LANT: Norfolk, Virginia. PAC: Wahiawa, Hawaii.
Jacksonville, FL; San Diego, CA; Bahrain; Guam; Naples, Italy; Far East / Yokosuka, Japan; Sicily.
organizations.hint: Seven NCTS sites across the globe.

chainOfCommand.definition: Has overall authority and overall responsibility for the command's communications.
Officer overseeing the command's communications organization.
chainOfCommand.hint: The officer in charge of comms.

chainOfCommand.definition: Large-deck radio officer. On smaller ships the COMMO and RO may be the same person.
chainOfCommand.hint: Big-deck radio officer; may merge with COMMO on small ships.

chainOfCommand.definition: Highest qualified enlisted person in Radio, typically E4-E6. Ensures communications capabilities are accomplished per the command's mission and handles incoming/outgoing traffic, devices, and manual procedures.
Works for and supports the CWO; establishes and maintains required circuits and initiates action to restore or bypass failed equipment.

Prepare the command's communications plan; monitor equipment allocation; prepare and maintain the communications watch quarter and station bill; conduct communications training; prepare SOPs for the communications center.
Qualifications, operating procedures, logs, communications/network maintenance, deck watches, and damage-control responsibilities.
chainOfCommand.hint: Covers PQS, logs, maintenance, watches, and DC.

messageTypes.definition: General military messages from UNCLASSIFIED through TOP SECRET — normal/general official message traffic.
Associated with SI / Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) communications.
Rapid, short, fast reporting of critical events/situations to senior government decision-makers.

draftingRoles.definition: The command originating the message, e.g., ship/base/command. Identified by the name of the ship/base/command.
The person who drafts/writes the message.
The person authorized to release the message. Not everyone has release authority.
Originator needs/sponsors the message -> Drafter writes it -> Releaser authorizes it. The same person can sometimes perform all three roles.

specialHandling.definition: Handling marking associated with nuclear information.
No longer RD but still requires safeguarding.
specialHandling.hint: Used to be RD, still protect it.

specialHandling.definition: Unclassified material requiring encryption for transmission; information with potential intelligence value that does not meet classification criteria.
specialHandling.hint: Encrypt even though it is unclassified.

specialHandling.definition: Classified messages identified with a special project/subject. Examples include Limited Distribution, NATO Restricted, Personal For, and Allied Restricted.
A message used when shifting communications guard from one station/NCTAMS to another.
Used to advise of a situation that might cause significant disruption of tactical communications; associated with communications status reports.

addressing.definition: Provides accurate, secure, expedient communications for various classes of ships and flagships.
Name of a single command / one command.
Group addressing involving 16 or more commands / PLAs.
4 or more PLAs within the group sharing a chain of command.

genserFormatLines.definition: Coded message header with defined character positions: first 2 letters are header characters (often TT), 4th character is classification (U/C/S/T), positions 5-8 are the Content Indicator Code (CIC), positions 9 and 21 are blank spaces, 10-15 are OSRI, 17-20 are SSN, 22-24 are Julian Date, 25-28 are Time Filed, 29-33 are classification repeated, 34 is Routing Indicator, and the final character is a period.

details.classification: U = Unclassified, C = Confidential, S = Secret, T = Top Secret.
details.colors: U = green, C = blue, S = red, T = orange.

genserFormatLines.definition: First three letters identify security handling. ZNR = unclassified; ZNY = classified.
Day / hour / minute / time zone / month / year. Format example: DDHHMMZ MON YY, where Z indicates Zulu time.
Originator — the command sending the message.
Action addressee — who the message is directed to and who must act.
Information addressee — receives the message for awareness; similar to a CC.
Break separating heading/address information from the message body.
Actual message body. Common components are SUBJ (Subject), REF (Reference), AMPN (Amplification - used when there is only one reference), NARR (Narrative), and RMKS (Remarks).
Sequence/serial number; number of the message per month.

operatingSignals.definition: Interrogative form asking for acknowledgment / whether a transmission was received.
I acknowledge / I received your transmission.
Interrogative signal used as the start of a procedural exchange.
Response shown in the notes to the INT QBZ example.

operationalNotes.definition: Protection of communications and associated information/material.
Advises the CO on physical security and handling of crypto/CMS publications and materials; manages the CMS account; controls storage; performs required reporting.
Before assuming the watch, complete inventory with two people: the person assuming the watch and a witness.
No erasures allowed. Records new radio day, watch turnover, messages received, circuit status, inventories, and significant events.
Condition used when communications capacity must be conserved; limit messages to roughly 100-200 words, emphasizing FLASH and IMMEDIATE traffic.
operationalNotes.hint: Conserve bandwidth; short and urgent only.

operationalNotes.definition: Tells you step-by-step how to perform a procedure.
Associated with communications/network maintenance, deck watches, and damage control qualifications.
